name: Acetyl glucosamine

card.summary: N-acetylglucosamine (NAG), an amino sugar used in skincare for brightening and gentle exfoliation to even tone and smooth skin texture.
card.note: Cosmetic skin products are widely available; individual skin sensitivity varies.

quick.overview:
Acetyl glucosamine, usually written N-acetylglucosamine (NAG or GlcNAc), is an amino sugar made by the body and used as an ingredient in skincare products. It is marketed for brightening skin tone and gently exfoliating.

The appearance payoff people look for is a more even, smoother-looking complexion. It is often found in serums and moisturisers alongside ingredients such as niacinamide.
quick.how: It is used in leave-on skincare products applied to the face, usually as part of a regular routine. Results are described as gradual and tied to continued use.
quick.risks: Cosmetic use is generally described as well tolerated, though any skincare ingredient can irritate sensitive skin. Product labels and a dermatologist are the reference for individual cases.

lead: N-acetylglucosamine is an amide derivative of glucose. In the body it is a building block of glycosylation, of bacterial cell walls and of chitin, and polymerised with glucuronic acid it forms hyaluronan.[1][2]

In skincare it is marketed under the name NAG or acetyl glucosamine as an ingredient for brightening and exfoliation, aimed at evening skin tone. Its link to hyaluronan, the molecule that holds water in skin, is part of why it is discussed in cosmetic formulation.[1]

Research on the compound is mostly biochemical: reviews describe the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway that makes the activated form of GlcNAc, and how dietary glucosamine and N-acetylglucosamine feed that pathway.[3]

chain: Gentle exfoliation and brightening action as marketed
angle.text: NAG is used in leave-on skincare with the aim of evening skin tone and improving texture. Products position it as a gentle alternative to stronger exfoliating actives.

infobox: Glycosylation; hyaluronan and chitin building block

paras: GlcNAc is a secondary amide between glucosamine and acetic acid. It is the first sugar attached to asparagine in N-linked glycosylation and a component of peptidoglycan, chitin and fungal cell walls. Polymerised with glucuronic acid, it forms hyaluronan.[1]

The hexosamine biosynthesis pathway produces UDP-GlcNAc, used for N- and O-linked glycosylation; the O-GlcNAc modification of proteins regulates signalling, transcription and other cell functions.[2][3][4]
Skincare products market NAG for brightening and exfoliation, and it is frequently combined with other ingredients in serums. Wikipedia's chemistry entry does not describe cosmetic applications.
No studies found. Related laboratory work examines the hexosamine pathway and notes that dietary supplementation with glucosamine and GlcNAc may reprogram metabolism.[3]
